title: test:changed has the same zero-selection ambiguity, flagged twice and never actioned
description:
Surfaced by TASK-192's seam audit as the one seam in its class that fell outside that ticket's file scope. This is the third time the defect class has been confirmed and the **second time this specific instance has been flagged** — it was raised in a deep-review synthesis on 2026-07-06 (recorded as R23 in `state/sessions/20260524T000000Z-65fa92c6/artifacts/deep-review-synthesis-2026-07-06.md`) and never actioned.

**The defect.** `npm run test:changed` compares against `HEAD`, so it selects only UNCOMMITTED changes — it selects zero specs once a diff is committed, and zero specs on a clean tree. A zero-selection run is visually indistinguishable from a run where everything passed. `CLAUDE.md` documents the behaviour ("it selects zero specs once the diff is committed"), but a developer running it after committing gets a green-looking result that verified nothing.

TASK-192 closed exactly this ambiguity for `test:since` by adding self-describing `TEST_SINCE_ZERO_SELECTION` markers to `scripts/test-since.mjs`, distinguishing `reason=empty-diff` from `reason=no-spec-matched` without changing the exit code. `test:changed` has no wrapper at all — it is a bare `vitest --changed` invocation in `package.json`, so there is nowhere for a marker to live today.

**Why it matters more than it looks.** `test:changed` is the FIRST command in the per-ticket hand-off gate. A developer who commits and then runs it as a final check gets a confident green from a run that selected nothing. That is the precise sequence a careful developer would follow.

**Follow the precedent, and follow the amendment that shaped it.** TASK-192's implementer first built a hard-fail version and had to revert it: a docs-only diff legitimately selects zero specs, so a blanket non-zero exit would red-gate every docs ticket. **Do not repeat that mistake here.** The goal is a self-describing empty, not a fatal one. Read `scripts/test-since.mjs`'s header comment and the "Empty-result contract" section of `CLAUDE.md` before designing anything — both were written specifically to record that reasoning.

Note the difference from `test:since`: for `test:changed`, the "clean tree / already committed" case is the COMMON one and is entirely legitimate, so the marker matters more than any failure ever could.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first demonstrates the ambiguity: `npm run test:changed` on a clean tree (or immediately after committing a diff) currently produces output indistinguishable from a successful verification run. Capture the red-run output verbatim.

The seam is made self-describing following the TASK-192 precedent: a caller can tell 'zero because nothing is uncommitted' from 'zero because the selection failed' without inferring it. Reuse the marker shape and reasoning already established in scripts/test-since.mjs rather than inventing a second convention.

The change MUST NOT make a zero selection fatal. A clean tree is the common and legitimate case for this command, and a hard failure would red-gate ordinary use — the same over-application TASK-192 built and had to revert. State explicitly in the closing comment that this was considered and rejected.

The real vitest exit code is passed through unchanged — verify that a genuine test FAILURE still exits non-zero after the change. A wrapper that swallows failures would be far worse than the ambiguity it fixes.

Any added pre-check does not meaningfully slow the inner development loop. test:changed is the fast iteration command; measure the added latency and record it. If the cost is material, prefer a cheaper signal over a thorough one.
Regression locks cover both branches (zero-selection marker present; normal selection produces no marker), red-green planted.
npm run test:all is green; no existing spec regresses; CLAUDE.md's Empty-result contract section is extended to record this instance alongside the three already listed.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
SCOPE ADDITION from TASK-192's full-depth review (MEDIUM-2), folded here because this ticket will reuse the same detection code.

**Nothing pins `hasAnyChangedFiles` to vitest's own `--changed` algorithm across upgrades.**

`scripts/test-since.mjs:109-125` reimplements vitest's change detection by issuing the identical three git commands vitest 2.1.9's `VitestGit` issues: `diff --name-only <ref>...HEAD`, `diff --cached --name-only`, and `ls-files --other --modified --exclude-standard`. The reviewer verified the mirror is verbatim TODAY. It is not pinned for tomorrow.

Two specific rot risks: the in-code comment cites a content-hash-named chunk (`node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/git.B5SDxu-n.js`) whose filename changes on the next vitest bump, and no sensor asserts the three command arrays still match what vitest actually runs.

**Blast radius is bounded, which is why it is MEDIUM and not HIGH.** Drift can only produce a wrong reason LABEL, never a wrong exit code — the `no-spec-matched` decision itself comes from vitest's own `vitest list --changed`, so the mirror only ever picks BETWEEN the two markers. But the label is the whole deliverable of that seam, so a silently-wrong reason defeats the purpose.

**Suggested fix, cheap:** a fast-tier spec that globs `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/git.*.js` (glob, not the hashed name) and asserts the three git-argument sequences still appear. That survives a version bump and fails loudly when vitest changes its algorithm.

Since this ticket implements the equivalent detection for `test:changed`, doing both under one mechanism — and pinning both with one sensor — is cheaper than solving it twice. Treat it as in scope here rather than minting a third ticket.

**Also inherited: the measured cost.** TASK-192's `vitest list` pre-check adds 5.2s to every `test:since` run with a non-empty diff. This ticket's AC5 already requires measuring the added latency for `test:changed` — note that `test:changed` is the FAST iteration command, run far more often than `test:since`, so the same 5s would be a materially worse trade there. If the cost lands anywhere near that, prefer a cheaper signal over a thorough one, exactly as AC5 says.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
APPROVED and closed on a green independent review.

**Review depth: FULL.** Rubric inputs: ~403 changed lines (387+/16-) across 7 files; touched surface is **the verification gate itself** (`scripts/test-since.mjs` refactored, new `scripts/test-changed.mjs`, `package.json` wiring for both). A defect here masks test failures repo-wide, and CLAUDE.md independently mandates `test:all` for test-infrastructure tickets.

**Findings: 0 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM / 2 LOW.** All discharged below; none blocking.

## AC3 — fatal-on-zero considered and REJECTED (stated here as the AC requires)

Making a zero selection fatal was considered and deliberately rejected. A clean tree is the **common, legitimate state** for `test:changed` — arguably more so than for `test:since`, since it is run constantly during normal iteration. A hard failure would red-gate ordinary use and force a manual override on every docs-only or clean-tree run, which is alarm fatigue that weakens the control rather than strengthening it. This is precisely the design TASK-192 built, discovered to be wrong, and reverted before hand-off; repeating it here would have repeated that mistake. The marker makes the reason **self-describing**, not fatal. Verified independently by the reviewer against a disposable clean-tree fixture: exit 0 with `TEST_CHANGED_ZERO_SELECTION: reason=empty-diff` on stderr.

## AC5 — the cost trade, measured twice

The `vitest list` pre-check that `test:since` uses costs ~5.2s and exists solely to distinguish `no-spec-matched` from `empty-diff`. It was deliberately **not** ported. `test:changed` is the fast inner-loop command, run far more often, so that cost would be a materially worse trade than the ambiguity it closes.

- Developer measured the git-only check at **~94.1ms** (5 runs: 94.1/98.6/90.6/96.9/90.6)
- Reviewer independently measured **88.0ms** (5 runs: 91.5/87.7/76.3/109.0/75.4)
- Reviewer confirmed `vitest list` is genuinely absent from `scripts/test-changed.mjs`

**Accepted residual, stated plainly:** the `no-spec-matched` case — a non-empty uncommitted diff the import graph fails to route — still zero-selects silently for `test:changed`, exactly as it always has. This is an unchanged pre-existing gap, not a new one, and the documentation IS the mitigation. The reviewer hit it live during dogfooding (two stray uncommitted JSON files → no marker, zero specs, exit 0), which is a fair demonstration that marker-absence is a signal a caller must know how to read.

## AC4 — exit-code passthrough, proven independently

The single most dangerous failure mode here would be a wrapper that swallows a real test failure. The reviewer did NOT accept the spec's own assertion as proof of itself — it built a disposable fixture with a genuinely failing uncommitted test and confirmed **exit 1** through the wrapper, no marker, `1 failed` on stdout.

## TASK-192 survived the disclosed git mishap — verified line by line

The developer disclosed that a mid-implementation `git checkout -- scripts/test-since.mjs` reverted that file to its **pre-ticket committed baseline** rather than restoring an in-memory edit; it caught this, reapplied the refactor via `Edit`, and reverified. Because a silent loss here would have re-opened a closed ticket's defect while every test still passed, the reviewer diffed the file against `120b380` and confirmed each TASK-192 guarantee individually:

- `resolveSafeRef` (`:77-99`) byte-identical — usage error, `rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}`, refusal message, `~0` non-numeric forwarding
- Loud non-zero exit on unresolvable ref (`:159-166`) identical
- BOTH markers identical: `reason=empty-diff` (`:197-202`) and `reason=no-spec-matched` + `vitest list` pre-check (`:178-195`), including the `matched` predicate
- `hasAnyChangedFiles` refactored onto `anyGitCommandReportsChange` but behaviorally identical — same three git-arg arrays, same conservative `status !== 0 || stdout non-empty` predicate treating a git failure as "might have changes"
- Exit-code passthrough (`:204-215`) identical

**Nothing was lost.** Disclosing the mishap rather than hiding it is what made this verifiable — exactly the right call by the developer.

## Folded scope — the vitest-algorithm pin, confirmed NON-VACUOUS

`tests/vitest-changed-algorithm-pin.spec.js` globs `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/git.*.js` (glob, never the hashed name), so it survives a version bump. The reviewer applied the TASK-184 lesson and ran a **negative simulation**: swapping `--name-only` for `--name-status` in a drifted chunk copy fails both diff-sequence regexes, and removing the `typeof changedSince` branch fails the fourth test. The checked set is three hard-coded regexes plus one substring — **never derived from a fixture run**, so the TASK-184 empty-checked-set failure mode is structurally impossible here. And because `findVitestGitChunk()` runs inside each `it()` and asserts the glob count `.toBe(1)`, an absent `node_modules` is a loud red rather than a vacuous green.

## Shared extraction verified against vitest's source, not the comment

`node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/git.B5SDxu-n.js:19-38` — `findChangedFiles` branches on `typeof changedSince === "string"`, and the refless branch awaits only `getStagedFiles()` + `getUnstagedFiles()`. So `hasAnyUncommittedChanges` dropping `GIT_DIFF_SINCE_ARGS` is an exact mirror of vitest's own refless behavior. The pin spec's fourth test locks that branch.

## Marker naming — reuse, not a second convention (AC2)

`TEST_CHANGED_ZERO_SELECTION` was the right call. The convention TASK-192 established is the **shape** — `<COMMAND>_ZERO_SELECTION: reason=<token>` on stderr — and the `empty-diff` reason token is reused verbatim. A `TEST_SINCE_`-prefixed marker emitted from `test:changed` would mislead anyone grepping stderr and falsely imply a ref was involved.

## Tier audit

`tests-after` is defensible; `tdd` was not required. Under the narrowed rubric `tdd` is reserved for security-sensitive logic, parsing, schema changes, or state mutation with edge-risk — this is a stateless selection wrapper, provable by running it. It also matches the TASK-192 precedent (same subsystem, same tier). The substance `tdd` exists to guarantee was delivered anyway via AC1's captured red run and AC6's red-green plants.

## MEDIUM discharged — hand-off artifacts DO exist

The reviewer reviews cold and was not given the developer hand-off, so it correctly logged that it could not confirm the agility-R3 checklist or AC1's verbatim red-run capture, and asked the Orchestrator to confirm or record. **Confirming: both exist in the hand-off.**

AC1 red-run, captured verbatim before any change:
```
> vitest run --changed --config vitest.config.all.js
 RUN  v2.1.9 C:/Fun/hivemind/hivemind
include:  tests/**/*.spec.js
No test files found, exiting with code 0
EXIT_CODE=0
```
Exit 0, output indistinguishable from a successful run — the defect demonstrated.

Agility-R3 checklist, all five items stated: (1) unspecced path exercised — ran `tests/e2e/test-since.spec.js`, the neighboring wrapper's full suite sharing the refactored module; (2) every new lock red-green planted — three groups, each restored via targeted `Edit`; (3) `dist/` rebuild N/A — no bundled `src/`/`bin/` touched, dist-parity green under `test:all`; (4) parity copies N/A — no agent/skill files touched; (5) calibration markers N/A — no `[ASSUMED]`/`[INFERRED:weak]` claims carried into code or docs.

AC6 red-green plants, each confirmed failing for the right reason then restored: stubbing `hasAnyUncommittedChanges` to `return false` reddened 3 of 4 new assertions (`expected false to be true`, `expected +0 to be 2`); inverting the marker condition reddened all 3 e2e tests (marker on the wrong branch); corrupting one regex to `--cached-PLANTED-BUG` reddened the targeted pin assertion naming the missing sequence.

## Gate

- `npm run test:since -- 120b380` — GREEN, 177 files / 2030 tests, non-zero selection
- `npm test` — GREEN, 81 files / 1087 passed, 2 skipped, 2.61s
- `tests/e2e/test-changed.spec.js` + `tests/e2e/test-since.spec.js` — GREEN, 8 tests
- `tests/test-since.spec.js` + `tests/vitest-changed-algorithm-pin.spec.js` — GREEN, 17 tests
- `npm run test:all` — GREEN, 177 files / 2030 tests, exit 0 (includes dist-parity, graph-freshness, doc-locks)
- `npm run check:calibration` — no violations

AC7's CLAUDE.md extension was checked for overstatement and does not overstate: instance 4's ~90ms figure, the absent `vitest list` pre-check, and the "accepted, unchanged" framing of the `no-spec-matched` gap all match the code and the reviewer's own measurements.
